terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s phrase, plain Latin, which it marks with a query.

terms.grammar: phrase: diplōma, diplōmatis n., with the genitive of ingressus
terms.comment: Our description, on the pattern of the passport, commeātūs diplōma (Traupman 217): a diplōma is an official permit (see licence), and ingressus an entering, used by Pliny of his arrival in his province (in ipsō ingressū meō, Plin. Ep. ad Traj. 17.4, in Lewis & Short). Kept beside Morgan–Owens’s phrase, because that names the permission and this the document.

sources: Lewis & Short: diploma · Lewis & Short: ingressus · Lewis & Short: licentia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 217.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. passport: visa.
